scope: Final full-scene park stops 0–5 in day and night; excludes museum, connecting flyby and motion performance.
method: All 12 listed PNGs were opened with view_image and actually inspected. Corrected Pavilion stop 3 was reviewed first in both modes. These are unfiltered progressive renders; no image edits or new renders were performed for this review.
findings: Corrected Pavilion ribbons expose broad curved steel faces above a dark stage cavity; trellis, suspended speakers, lawn and stage composition read clearly in both modes. Violet/warm nighttime lighting keeps the headdress and stage visible.

Overview shows the mapped spatial relationship among Grainger Plaza, Crown Fountain, Monument, Great Lawn, Lurie Garden, BP Bridge and Nichols Bridgeway. Night illumination identifies plaza, stage, lawn and principal paths.

Cloud Gate outer and underside views have continuous curved skyline/paving reflections and a clear arch opening. The former scalloped normal artifact is absent. Warm plaza light makes the lower mirrored shell readable against a dark blue upper shell at night.
Crown Fountain framing is unobstructed; glass-block joints, stream silhouette and reflected tower/pool illumination are visible in day and night.
Lurie Garden beds, paths, hedges, flowers and the Nichols connection remain readable in the final camera composition, with stronger foreground lighting at night.
limitations: Unfiltered 128/256-sample stills retain Monte Carlo grain, especially in reflected paving and dark surfaces. This still-image review does not certify motion noise performance.
Tree crowns use simplified solid geometry; foreground garden trees look stylized and brightly lit at night. Flower species and individual planting specimens are authored approximations.
Cloud Gate and Pritzker ribbons are reference-based geometric interpretations, not scans or fabrication CAD; the Pavilion headdress is simplified.
Crown LED imagery is an original abstract color field, not the actual filmed portraits. Water geometry is static and the narrow stream reads as a dark silhouette; ripple shading is an approximation.
Surrounding city footprints follow map data, while many facades retain generic repeated windows and simplified architectural treatment.
Light positions, beam angles and powers are authored for visual correspondence; this is not surveyed photometry.
